info.title: Jalachakra API
info.description:
Crop water requirement prediction and irrigation decision support.

**What the numbers mean.** `cwr_mm_day` is crop water *demand*: what the crop will transpire. `net_irrigation_mm` is what must reach the root zone after rainfall. `gross_irrigation_mm` is what must be *delivered*, and is always the larger figure because no irrigation system is fully efficient. These are three different quantities and the API never conflates them.

**What the model was trained on.** A FAO-56 reference-derived crop evapotranspiration, not observed field water use. No independently observed water requirement exists in this project's data, and `/api/v1/data-quality/summary` says so in the response.

post.description:
Create an account and its farmer profile in one step.

A user without a farmer profile cannot own a farm, so creating the two
together removes a state the rest of the API would have to guard against.

Client-side logout.

Tokens are stateless and self-expiring, so there is nothing to revoke
server-side without a denylist. Saying so is better than implying a
server-side session that does not exist.

Every crop the system can model.

A crop appears here only if it has a complete four-stage coefficient curve.
Offering a crop the system cannot actually compute would produce a confusing
failure later in the prediction flow.

Development and late-season values are interpolated rather than tabulated,
so this is a continuous curve rather than four steps.

post.description:
Recalculate the requirement under different assumptions.

This is the what-if tool: take an existing prediction and ask what changes
if the irrigation system were more efficient, or if forecast rain is counted.
The stored prediction is not modified, so the original advice stays intact.
Log an irrigation event, and mirror it into the water-use ledger.

get.description:
Predicted demand against water actually applied.

The balance is the number worth looking at: persistent over-application
wastes water, persistent under-application stresses the crop. It compares a
modelled demand with a farmer-reported application, so it is a planning
indicator rather than a measurement of either quantity.
The most recent advice across all of this farmer's plantings.

What the system knows about the trustworthiness of its own inputs.

Surfacing this in the app is deliberate. A farmer acting on an estimate
built from estimated inputs should be able to see that.

post.description:
Rank crops on agronomic suitability and on whether the water exists to grow them.

Suitability alone can recommend a crop the farmer cannot water. This combines
both and states the trade-off rather than hiding it behind a single score.

get.description:
What this deployment can answer, and on what evidence.

The interface calls this before offering a feature, so a farmer is told
"this deployment has no price data" rather than shown an empty column and
left to guess whether the crops are worthless or the data is missing.

schema.title: Response Coverage Api V1 Water Intelligence Coverage Get

get.description:
Rank crops by what they return per unit of water consumed.

Two productivities are reported because they answer different questions:
kilograms per cubic metre transpired (what the plant achieves) and per
cubic metre delivered (what the farmer achieves, after irrigation losses).
Value per cubic metre uses the annual minimum support price rather than the
three-day market snapshot this project happens to hold.

post.description:
What a finite seasonal water budget will actually grow.

The farmer states the water they can get - a borewell's seasonal yield, a
tank, a canal allocation - and the plot they want to grow on. Each crop is
assessed against that volume: whether it finishes the plot, and if not, how
much of the plot it does finish.

A crop the budget cannot complete is reported with its irrigable area
rather than dropped, because growing a smaller area properly is a real
decision and this endpoint exists to inform it.

get.description:
Recent rainfall for a district, against its long-period normal.

Supply ``farm_id``, or ``state`` and ``district``. The rainfall file covers
twenty days, so this is current-season context - departure from normal and
dry-spell length - and the response says so rather than letting it be read
as a trend.

PredictionOut.title: PredictionOut
PredictionOut.description:
The core response.

Demand and irrigation requirement are separate fields, and net and gross are
separate fields, because collapsing either pair is how this kind of system
gives wrong advice.

WeatherInputSchema.title: WeatherInputSchema
WeatherInputSchema.description:
Weather supplied directly by the caller.

Wind and radiation are optional because a farmer rarely has either. When
they are absent the baseline substitutes documented FAO-56 values and the
response says which inputs were estimated.
